data.long_meaning: In Greek, Rowe means red, derived from the color of the ripe rowan berries. In Scottish folklore, the rowan tree is believed to protect against evil. Parents who choose Rowe usually hope their child will grow to embody red, rowan tree and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rowe has its origins in the Greek language, where it translates to red. In Anglo-Saxon culture, Rowe was a byname for someone with red hair, or a nickname for someone with red or rosy complexion. Over time, the name gained popularity as a personal name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Scottish folklore, the rowan tree is believed to be a symbol of protection against evil. The name Rowe, derived from the Greek word for red, is also associated with the vibrant color of rowan berries. The spiritual significance of the name Rowe can be interpreted as a reminder of the protective power of God, as symbolized by the rowan tree in Scottish folklore. It can also represent the redemptive power of Christ, as depicted in His blood, which was shed for the salvation of humanity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Rowe in Christianity is derived from the Old English word 'rēowan,' meaning 'to plow.' It symbolizes the faithful Christian's call to till God's earth, cultivate virtues, and sow seeds of wisdom and love. Additionally, Rowe can be seen as a reminder to dig deep into one's spiritual beliefs, unearthing the treasures hidden in the soul.
